nodes.summary: Glauberman's $Z^*$-theorem. Let $G$ be a finite group and let $t \in G$ be an involution ($t \neq 1$ and $t^2 = 1$) such that every conjugate $g t g^{-1}$ of $t$ that commutes with $t$ equals $t$. Then there is a normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ of odd order such that $g t g^{-1} t^{-1} \in N$ for every $g \in G$.
nodes.title: Glauberman's $Z^*$-theorem

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, $O(G)$ is the join, in the lattice of subgroups of $G$, of all normal subgroups $N$ of $G$ such that every element of $N$ has finite odd order. In a periodic group this join is again a normal subgroup consisting of elements of odd order, so it is the largest such subgroup.
nodes.title: Odd core from normal subgroups of odd-order elements

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, let $O(G)$ be the join of all normal subgroups of $G$ all of whose elements have odd order. There exist a periodic group $G$ and an involution $i \in G$ such that $g^{-1} i g i$ has odd order for every $g \in G$, but the image of $i$ in $G / O(G)$ is not central: $g i g^{-1} i^{-1} \notin O(G)$ for some $g \in G$. This answers Kourovka Problem 11.13 in the negative.
nodes.title: A periodic counterexample to Borovik's question (Kourovka 11.13)

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, let $O(G)$ be the join of all normal subgroups of $G$ all of whose elements have odd order. This is the statement that for every periodic group $G$ and every involution $i \in G$ such that $g^{-1} i g i$ has odd order for every $g \in G$, the image of $i$ in $G / O(G)$ is central, that is, $g i g^{-1} i^{-1} \in O(G)$ for every $g \in G$.
nodes.title: Borovik's question on involutions with odd-order products (Kourovka 11.13)
